info.description: camus-cli is a command-line interface for interacting with CamusDB

options.name: --connection-source
options.description:
Connection string (default: gRPC on
http://localhost:5096,
falling back to REST on http://localhost:5095)

options.name: --execute
options.description:
Execute a SQL statement (or ;-separated
statements) and exit

options.name: --file
options.description:
Execute the statements in a .sql file and exit;
stops at the
first error. Use -f - to read the script from
standard input

options.name: --user
options.description:
User to authenticate as (only needed on a server
with
authentication enabled)

options.name: --password
options.description:
That user's password; prompted for when -u is
given without it

options.name: --token
options.description:
Use a bearer token obtained elsewhere instead of
logging in

options.name: --tui
options.description:
Open the full-screen browser: catalog, editor
and results
in three panes. TAB moves between panes, F5 runs
the query

options.name: --force-rich
options.description:
Force the rich line editor (colors, multiline,
Tab completion)
on terminals whose TERM value Spectre.Console
doesn't recognize

options.name: --diagnose-terminal
options.description:
Print terminal capabilities and exit (why rich
mode is on/off)

options.name: --help
options.description: Show this help message

options.name: --version
options.description:
Show version information
Environment variables:
CAMUS_FORCE_RICH=1            Same as --force-rich (accepts 1/true/yes)
CAMUS_USER                    Default for -u
CAMUS_PASSWORD                Default for -p (keeps the password out of the
shell history)
CAMUS_ACCESS_TOKEN            Default for --token

-u, --user / -p, --password   Credentials for an authenticated server
Shell commands:
use <database>              Switch the current database; the name may be
`backticked`. Works in script files too
source <file> [--force]     Run the statements in a file, streaming it;
--force carries on past failures
show prepared [sql]         What the driver keeps prepared; with SQL, whether
that
statement is prepared (alias: \prepared)
clear / exit / quit         Clear the screen / leave the shell
Cluster settings: (SQL, not shell commands; each runs without a current
database)
show variables [like '<pattern>']
This node's effective configuration, with each
setting's mutability (runtime|restart) and scope
show cluster settings [like '<pattern>']
What the cluster overlay currently carries
set cluster setting <key> = <value>
Change a runtime setting fleet-wide, from any
node
reset cluster setting <key>   Drop the overlay entry; each node resolves the
key
through its own config again
Introspection: (SQL, not shell commands)
show statistics for [table] <name>
What the optimizer believes about a table: row
counts,
column min/max, histogram buckets,
distinct-value counts,
and how stale they are (analyze <table>
refreshes them)
show ranges from table <name>
show ranges from index <table>@<index>
How a relation's key space is divided into
spans, and
where each span's leader is, as this node sees
it
show range from table <name> for row (<primary key>)
show range from index <table>@<index> for row (<values>)
The one span that holds a row. Fifteen columns,
so
append \G for vertical output
show engine stats             Runtime engine metrics for the node answering
show slow queries [like '<pattern>']
What this node recorded over its slow-query
threshold,
newest first. Off by default, and lost on
restart;
fourteen columns, so append \G for vertical
output
